newsitem.title: UK: London gold keeps tenuous grip above key $380.
newsitem.headline: London gold keeps tenuous grip above key $380.

text.p: The gold market was choppy and nervous on Thursday afternoon with gold holding just above the critical $380 an ounce level, dealers said.
Bullion fixed at $380.70 an ounce, compared to the morning fix of $383.30 which was a fresh low since Sept 6, 1995. Bids had briefly dipped below $380, with a low quote of $379.70.
"There's been a concerted attempt to go after the $380 level in gold, but it's held so far," a dealer said. "This is a real key area for gold and the key for the whole sector."
Comex December gold was down $0.60 at $383.00 an ounce, up from an early low of $381.90 on end-quarter fund shortcovering.
The proximity to the psychological $380, and technical $379 levels gave an edge to trading. "The gold fix and the New York close are the key times for gold," a dealer said.
In the case of a break below $379, gold was expected to find some support at $375, then at $372, dealers said. Some analysts have forecast a move as low as $360.
"The critical support immediately below $380 has held and is indicated to continue to do so for now," analyst Elli Gifford of Investent Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
"However, recovery prospects are poor...A breakdown would herald falls to $370 at least," she added.

The market was still jumpy after International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus said on Thursday the IMF had a necessary majority to sell five million ounces gold to help pay for aid to poor countries.
However, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the sales may not be needed until the year 2000.
"Camdessus didn't clear up the situation at all. He says the IMF has the mandate to sell gold, but doesn't say if, when or how much," a dealer said.
Fresh tensions in the Middle East were not seen providing any visible support for gold so far.
Dealers noted that a rise in lease rates was a result of some producer selling along with bullion banks adjusting positions ahead of the end of the year accounts.
Silver was indicated at $4.92/$4.94 an ounce, up four cents from Thursday's London closing level and watching gold closely.
Platinum was off the day's lows at $385.25/$386.25, up $0.25 from Thursday's close. Palladium was stronger at $118.75/$119.75, up $1.50.
"Platinum and silver really depend on gold, and if gold goes, then they will as well," a dealer said.
